wgAim: Whole Genome Analyses via Integrated Modelling

Source: R/wgAim-package.R
wgAim-package.Rd

The wgAim package provides a unified framework for whole-genome analysis in plant breeding populations, built entirely around the ASReml-R linear mixed modelling engine. It extends and supersedes the legacy wgaim package, broadening the scope from QTL detection alone into three integrated analytical pillars:

qtlAim

Forward-selection QTL detection in biparental mapping populations using whole-genome average interval mapping. Supports fixed and random QTL effects, interval or marker selection, and multivariate models via the Trait argument (trials, environments, sites, treatments, or measured traits).

gwasAim

Forward-selection genome-wide association analysis in diversity panels. Uses the same composite genome-wide model as qtlAim with marker effects always treated as fixed. Supports multivariate models via the Trait grouping argument.

gpAim

Genomic best linear unbiased prediction (G-BLUP) delivering genomic estimated breeding values (GEBVs) and BLUP accuracies via either a genomic relationship matrix (vm path) or direct marker-by-file random effects (mbf path). Supports univariate and multivariate models via Trait.

The genomic prediction pillar is completed by selIndex, which combines per-environment GEBVs from a multivariate gpAim fit into a single selection index (weighted, Smith-Hazel, or Pesek-Baker desired-gains), computes expected genetic gain, and provides diagnostic plots for adaptation screening.

Details

Shared engine: All three analyses share a common internal engine. The unifying statistical idea is that the full complement of markers or intervals is included simultaneously in the mixed model as a composite genome-wide random effect, represented either as a genomic relationship matrix (vm path, when markers exceed lines) or as a marker-by-file random effect (mbf path, when lines equal or exceed markers).

Multivariate extensions (Trait argument): All three analysis functions accept an optional Trait argument naming a factor column in the phenotypic data that defines the grouping structure for multivariate analysis — trials, environments, sites, treatments, or measured traits. When supplied, a multivariate model is fitted using mixture chi-squared LRT for significance testing and Wald test pruning to classify QTL as main effects or group-by-genotype interactions. The variance structure of the additive genomic term is controlled by the str argument ("corh", "fa1", etc.).

Data preparation:

  • Biparental mapping populations: use primeCross to prepare a "wgCross" object from an R/qtl cross object. fixMap and imputeGen() are available as helpers for map and genotype quality control.

  • Diversity panels: use primePanel to prepare a "wgPanel" object from a raw marker matrix.

Supporting functions:

  • fineMap – high-resolution scan around a detected QTL or association.

  • aimTable – stack summary tables from multiple qtlAim or gwasAim objects (multi-trait comparison).

  • aimTrace – trace the forward-selection algorithm: LRT statistics, QTL effect stability plots.

  • linkMap – genetic linkage map plots annotated with detected QTL or GWAS markers.

  • getQTL – extract QTL position and flanking marker information from a fitted object.

Bundled datasets: Three biparental wheat populations with paired genotype/phenotype data are included: RAC875 x Kukri (genoRxK / phenoRxK), Cascades x RAC875-2 (genoCxR / phenoCxR), and Sunco x Tasman (genoSxT / phenoSxT).

References

Verbyla, A.P., Cullis, B.R. and Thompson, R. (2007). The analysis of QTL by simultaneous use of the full linkage map. Theoretical and Applied Genetics, 116, 95–111.

Verbyla, A.P., Taylor, J.D. and Verbyla, K.L. (2012). RWGAIM: An efficient high-dimensional random whole genome average (QTL) interval mapping approach. Genetics Research, 94, 291–306.

Taylor, J. and Verbyla, A.P. (2011). R Package wgaim: QTL Analysis in Bi-Parental Populations Using Linear Mixed Models. Journal of Statistical Software, 40(7), 1–18.
